analysis.title: Goldman 2027 playbook: AI capex, momentum unwind and quant rebound
key_insights: Goldman Sachs estimates annualized US AI investment will reach $1.4 trillion by the end of 2027, as the AI spending boom widens from semiconductors to an economy-wide capex cycle.
Since ChatGPT launched, AI has accounted for 21% of US GDP growth, 62% of earnings growth and 92% of market value growth (GIR), so the market impact is far larger than the real-economy impact so far.

JPMorgan estimates each additional $100B of AI capex adds about $9 to 2027 S&P 500 EPS, or 2.5% earnings growth. At the midpoint of its spending assumptions that is roughly $18 of upside to consensus EPS, adding 4-5 percentage points to earnings growth.
S&P 500 earnings are at a record share of US GDP (FactSet). The open question for 2027 is how much further the profit share can expand.

Forward P/E and PEG ratios are near their 35-year historical averages (Datastream). The note says this does not make equities cheap given today's concentration, but it weakens the blanket 'everything is a bubble' argument.
GS Prime Brokerage reports momentum exposure in its prime book has fallen to the 23rd percentile of the past five years. Hedge funds have cut it sharply from the crowded highs earlier this year.
Momentum volatility is significantly elevated relative to index volatility (Marquee).

Quant strategies had their biggest two-day comeback in almost three years after weeks of losses. GS PB attributes both days to renormalization of momentum (medium and short horizons) and recovery in crowded trades. The note frames the open question as a proper recovery versus another violent squeeze.
earnings_insights: JPMorgan: each additional $100B of AI capex adds about $9 of 2027 S&P 500 EPS (2.5% earnings growth). At the midpoint of its capex assumptions that is about $18 above consensus 2027 EPS, adding 4-5 percentage points to earnings growth.
AI accounts for 62% of US earnings growth since ChatGPT launched (GIR).
risk_factors: The quant rebound may be another violent squeeze rather than a durable recovery, in a market where momentum volatility is elevated.
Extreme equity concentration means valuations near 35-year averages do not make equities cheap.
The profit share of GDP is already at a record, which limits how much further it can expand in 2027.
AI's market impact (92% of market value growth) is far ahead of its real-economy contribution (21% of GDP growth).

tension_points.bull_case: JPMorgan estimates each additional $100B of AI capex adds about $9 to 2027 S&P 500 EPS, roughly $18 of upside to consensus at its midpoint. Forward P/E and PEG ratios are near 35-year averages, which weakens the bubble narrative.
tension_points.bear_case: Concentration is extreme, so near-average multiples do not make equities cheap. Earnings are already a record share of GDP, and AI has driven 92% of market value growth against 21% of GDP growth.

tension_points.bull_case: The quants' biggest two-day comeback in almost three years, driven by renormalization of momentum and recovery in crowded trades, could mark the start of a proper recovery.
tension_points.bear_case: The move could be another violent squeeze in a market that has 'forgotten how to trade quietly', with momentum volatility elevated relative to index volatility.
